options.value: ACT/365F
options.note: GBP and Commonwealth money markets quote ACT/365 Fixed

options.value: points / 10^4
points / 10^2

default: points / 10^4 (10^2 for JPY pairs)

options.value: F = S (1 + r_d tau_d) / (1 + r_f tau_f) (simple money-market rates)
options.note: each leg uses its own currency's day count

options.value: F = S exp((r_d - r_f) T) (continuous rates)

default: simple money-market rates with each currency's own day count
source: Hull OFOD ch.5; ISDA

default: the count the task states; otherwise the sampling frequency of the series (252 for daily trading data)
source: Bodie-Kane-Marcus ch.5; Lo (2002) The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios

options.value: mean(excess) / std(excess, ddof=1) * sqrt(periods)
mean / std with ddof=0
annualised mean / annualised vol (geometric return in the numerator)

default: arithmetic mean excess return over sample std (ddof=1), times sqrt(periods per year); risk-free 0 unless given
source: Sharpe (1994) J. Portfolio Mgmt; Lo (2002)

options.value: log returns ln(P_t/P_{t-1})
simple returns P_t/P_{t-1} - 1

default: simple returns for portfolio aggregation and P&L; log returns when the task names them
source: Campbell-Lo-MacKinlay (1997) ch.1

options.value: ddof=1 (sample)
ddof=0 (population)

default: ddof=1 for estimates from a sample; ddof=0 only when the task says population (cross-sectional z-scores often state it)
source: Casella-Berger s.5.2

options.value: order statistic: the ceil(n alpha)-th worst loss
linearly interpolated quantile (numpy 'linear')
lower/higher empirical quantile

default: the quantile method the task names; otherwise numpy's linear quantile of the loss distribution, reported as a positive loss
source: Jorion, Value at Risk (3rd ed.) ch.10; Hull RMFI ch.13

options.value: positive loss amount
negative return quantile

default: positive number = loss
source: Jorion ch.5; Basel market-risk framework

options.value: mean of losses at or beyond the VaR quantile
mean of the worst floor(n (1-alpha)) losses

default: average of the losses at or beyond VaR
source: Acerbi & Tasche (2002); Basel FRTB

options.value: square-root-of-time: VaR_h = VaR_1 * sqrt(h)
overlapping h-day returns

default: square-root-of-time from the 1-day VaR unless the task builds h-day returns
source: BCBS (1996) Amendment to the Capital Accord; Hull RMFI ch.13

options.value: max(VaR_{t-1}, m_c * mean(VaR over 60 days)) (+ stressed VaR term in Basel 2.5)
Basel 2.5: + max(sVaR_{t-1}, m_s * mean(sVaR 60d))

default: the formula the task gives; otherwise the BCBS 1996 / Basel 2.5 form with multiplier from the traffic-light table
source: BCBS (1996, 2009 Revisions to the Basel II market risk framework)

options.value: zero mean
constant mean mu

default: the mean model the task names; when the task is silent: the constant-mean equation r_t = mu + e_t (Bollerslev 1986 regression mean; Tsay ch.3; arch_model's default mean='Constant'), except a daily VaR / risk-capital model, which takes the RiskMetrics zero daily mean
source: Bollerslev (1986); Tsay, Analysis of Financial Time Series (3rd ed.) ch.3; RiskMetrics Technical Document (1996); arch documentation (arch_model mean='Constant' default)

decision: which rows are monthly rebalance dates

options.value: last OBSERVED trading day of each calendar month of the sample, the final (possibly partial) month included
options.note: the rows are the trading calendar when no exchange calendar is supplied; groupby(month).last()

options.value: complete calendar months only (a sample that ends mid-month has no rebalance in that month)
calendar month-end date (rebalance on the last calendar day, carried to the next trading row)

default: the last observed row of each calendar month in the sample (final month included); a window must be full before the first rebalance
source: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) J. Finance (month-end formation dates from the data's own calendar); DeMiguel, Garlappi & Uppal (2009) RFS (rolling-window monthly rebalancing)

decision: first return day of a lagged-weight backtest (no prior weight exists)

options.value: kept as a zero-return day (the missing lagged weight is 0) - series length = number of return dates
options.note: same treatment as the warm-up rows that carry no position

options.value: dropped - the series starts at the second return date
options.when: drop the first (?:return|row|day)|(?:series|backtest) starts? (?:at|on) the second

default: a day without a position earns 0 and stays in the evaluated series (positions shifted one bar, missing positions = 0)
source: Chan, Quantitative Trading (2009) ch.3 (lagged positions, missing positions earn zero); Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu (2014) on look-ahead

decision: what a count of 'signal days' counts in a cross-sectional long-short backtest

options.value: formation days: trading days on which enough names carry a valid signal to form the long-short book (>= long_n + short_n ranked names)
options.note: the formation dates of a sorted-portfolio backtest

options.value: every trading day of the price panel

default: the days on which the portfolio is formed from the signal
source: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) J. Finance (formation periods); Grinold & Kahn, Active Portfolio Management (2nd ed.) ch.6 (breadth counts the periods with a valid forecast)

decision: numerical scale for the GARCH likelihood

options.value: fit on 100 x returns, convert omega/1e4 and sigma/100
options.note: the likelihood is scale-equivariant; optimisers converge better on percent returns

options.value: fit on decimal returns
options.note: report in native units either way

default: maximise the likelihood (percent scale for the optimiser), report parameters in the units of the input
source: arch documentation (Sheppard); Bollerslev (1986)

options.value: lambda = 0.94 (daily)
lambda = 0.97 (monthly)

default: the decay the task states; RiskMetrics 0.94 daily / 0.97 monthly otherwise
source: J.P. Morgan RiskMetrics Technical Document (1996)

options.value: alpha = 2/(span+1), seeded with the first value (pandas ewm adjust=False)
alpha = 2/(span+1), seeded with the SMA of the first span values

default: alpha = 2/(span+1); the seed the task states, else the first observation
source: Murphy, Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets ch.9

options.value: trade at the next bar (positions lag the signal by one period)
same-bar execution when the signal already uses data up to t-1

default: a position earns the return after the information used to set it (no look-ahead)
source: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado (2014) Pseudo-mathematics and financial charlatanism

options.value: positive magnitude
options.note: know81: a 'decline' and a Calmar ratio reported next to it (return / max drawdown, Young 1991) use the magnitude

options.value: negative number
options.note: a formula dividing by |max_drawdown| or W/cummax(W) - 1 keeps the sign

default: the sign the task states; otherwise a negative fraction from peak
source: Magdon-Ismail & Atiya (2004) Maximum drawdown; Young (1991) Calmar ratio

decision: trading signal while an indicator is still undefined (warm-up rows)

options.value: binary: the comparison is simply false -> the 'otherwise' side (e.g. -1), every row traded
options.when: [-\u2212]1 otherwise|no [\"'\u201c]?no position[\"'\u201d]? state|always (?:long or short|in the market)
options.note: a two-state rule has no flat state, so undefined inputs fall to the else-branch

options.value: flat: weight 0 while undefined, the zero-return rows stay in the series
drop: the series starts at the first row with every indicator defined

default: the rule the task states; a signal defined as 'A when X, B otherwise' takes B while X is undefined
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) time-series momentum (sign rule, always +/-1); Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017) A century of evidence on trend-following

decision: which GARCH(1,1) volatility prices an option / structured product

options.value: long-run (unconditional) vol sqrt(A * omega / (1 - alpha - beta))
options.note: the constant sigma a constant-vol (Black-Scholes / Reiner-Rubinstein) formula takes

options.value: one-step conditional forecast vol sqrt(A * sigma2_{T+1})
term-structure vol: average expected variance over the option life
options.note: V_L + (V_0 - V_L)(1 - e^{-aT})/(aT), a = ln(1/(alpha + beta))

default: the vol the task names; when it reports only the GARCH parameters and their long-run variance, the long-run (unconditional) vol
source: Bollerslev (1986) unconditional variance; Hull OFOD ch.23 (GARCH volatility term structure)

decision: daily interest-carry accrual of a currency position in a carry backtest

options.value: differential_{t-1} x calendar days since the previous row / the investor's home money-market basis
options.note: one excess rate of a home-currency investor, accrued ACT/<home basis> (USD: ACT/360, day_counts file)

options.value: each leg on its own day count: r_f d/B_f - r_home d/B_home
differential_{t-1} / periods per year on every return row
options.when: (?:divided|divide) by (?:the )?(?:annuali[sz]ation factor|periods per year)|per trading day

default: interest accrues on calendar days (ACT) on the rate known at the start of the day
source: ISDA 2006 Definitions s.4.16 (ACT/360 USD money market); Lustig & Verdelhan (2007) carry excess return; Burnside, Eichenbaum, Kleshchelski & Rebelo (2011)

options.value: iid resampling with replacement
stationary block bootstrap

default: iid draws of standardised residuals (FHS) with the seed the task gives
source: Efron & Tibshirani (1993); Barone-Adesi, Giannopoulos, Vosper (1999); Politis & Romano (1994)

options.value: linear on zero rates
log-linear on discount factors (piecewise-flat forwards)
cubic spline on zero rates

default: the scheme the task names; otherwise linear on zero rates
source: Hagan & West (2006) Interpolation methods for curve construction

options.value: calendar days / 365
trading days / 252

default: calendar days / 365 unless the task states otherwise
source: Hull OFOD ch.15; Clark FX Option Pricing ch.1

options.value: modified following
following
preceding

default: modified following
source: ISDA 2006 Definitions s.4.12

options.value: centered: 1 - SSR / sum (y - mean y)^2
uncentered: 1 - SSR / sum y^2
options.note: only for the R2 the qualifier is attached to (e.g. 'total R² (uncentered)')

default: the centering the task names for EACH R2 (a qualifier binds only to the R2 it is attached to); an unqualified R2 next to a qualified one is the textbook centered R2 (know86: the IPCA 'every R2 against zero' reading was graded WRONG 4x)
source: Greene, Econometric Analysis s.3.5; Kelly, Pruitt, Su (2019) JFE

options.value: the lag the task states

default: the lag the task states; otherwise floor(4 (T/100)^(2/9))
source: Newey & West (1987, 1994)

options.value: the percentiles the task states, per cross-section

default: the stated percentiles, applied per date cross-section
source: Fama-French practice; Green, Hand, Zhang (2017)

options.value: f* = mu / sigma^2 (continuous-time growth optimum)
fractional Kelly c f*

default: f* = mu / sigma^2 with the cap the task states
source: Thorp (2006) The Kelly criterion in blackjack, sports betting and the stock market

options.value: KPS: Gamma'Gamma = I and F'F/T diagonal descending imposed in every ALS sweep, then the final eigen-rotation of F'F/T (F'F/T = diag(eigvals)) and the sign rule
options.note: the estimator's own identification; its final rotation is the scale the eigendecomposition produces

options.value: plain ALS (no identification inside the sweep), one eigen-rotation after convergence
options.note: only when the task orders it explicitly; the scale drifts with the initialisation

default: KPS identification in the sweep (Kelly, Pruitt, Su 2019 sec. 2); a plain ALS only when the task orders one
source: Kelly, Pruitt, Su (2019) JFE 'Characteristics are covariances'; ipca package (bkelly-lab)

options.value: flip each factor (and its Gamma column) with negative mean after every eigen-rotation, i.e. inside every sweep that carries the KPS identification, and once more after the final rotation
options.note: ipca package ALS step ('enforce sign convention' after the rotation); the sign rule resolves an eigendecomposition's sign freedom, so it follows each one; factors identical, the loop's convergence flag then describes the estimator (know87)

options.value: flip once, after the final rotation only
options.note: a plain ALS has no eigen step inside the sweep; with a KPS sweep the eigenvector signs then alternate and the literal loop never meets tol (flag False, count = max_iter)

default: after every eigen-rotation the estimator performs (ipca package); once only for a plain ALS or when the task forbids a per-sweep sign
source: Kelly, Pruitt, Su (2019) JFE sec. 2; ipca package (bkelly-lab) ALS step sign convention

options.value: round only where the task says, to the places it says

default: no rounding unless asked; never round intermediates
source: IEEE 754 / numerical practice

decision: end points of a trailing calendar-day window (events counted 'in the last w days')

options.value: (t - w, t]: right-closed, the w calendar days ending on t
options.note: pandas offset windows rolling('wD') default closed='right'

options.value: [t - w, t]: both ends inclusive (w + 1 calendar days)
[t - w, t): today excluded

decision: 'days since last event' when there is no (recent) event

options.value: missing (NaN) when there is no event, then the task's missing-value rule
days since the first available date (full history)

default: right-censored at the window length of the matching trailing features (no event -> w)
source: Klein & Moeschberger (2003) Survival Analysis, ch.3 (right censoring at the end of the observation window)

decision: liquidation score of a seller bucket (named by the task, formula not written)

days to liquidate (shares / ADV)

decision: conviction from the AIC gap between the best and second-best model

options.value: logistic 1 / (1 + exp(-gap / s)), in [0.5, 1)
re-centred 2 / (1 + exp(-gap / s)) - 1 = tanh(gap / 2s), zero at a tie (Akaike-weight margin w1 - w2 for s = 2)
Akaike weight of the best model exp(-d_i/2) / sum_j exp(-d_j/2)

default: the formula the task writes; the logistic of gap / scale when it only says 'sigmoid'
source: Burnham & Anderson (2002) Model Selection and Multimodel Inference s.2.9 (Akaike weights)

decision: difference of two reported figures (B - A, year over year)

options.value: exact decimal difference: b - a rounded to the decimal places of its inputs
raw binary floating-point difference

default: b - a rounded to the inputs' decimal places (int - int stays int)
source: Goldberg (1991) What every computer scientist should know about floating-point arithmetic, ACM Computing Surveys

decision: which rows form the trailing estimation window (covariance / volatility) used to size day t's positions

options.value: strictly prior bars: rows t-W .. t-1
options.note: helpers86_1.trailing_window_rule -> 'prior'; the sibling eigen-regime risk-parity estimator (trailing window R[t-W:t]) passed with it

options.value: up to and including day t: rows t-W+1 .. t
options.note: day t's close-to-close return is known at the close where the weights are set

default: the rows the task's words name; with no wording, rows t-W+1 .. t (the return of day t is known at its close)
source: RiskMetrics Technical Document (1996) sec. 5 (estimates from data available before the forecast); Moreira & Muir (2017) J. Finance (volatility-managed portfolios scale by the prior window)

decision: which close enters a cash dividend's backward price-adjustment factor (P - D)/P

options.value: the close ON the ex-dividend date (nearest prior trading day when the date is not in the series)
the cum-dividend close: the last close strictly before the ex-date
options.when: cum[- ]dividend close|(?:previous|prior|preceding|last) (?:trading )?(?:day'?s? )?close (?:before|prior to) the ex|close (?:on|of) the (?:trading )?day before the ex

default: the close the task's words name; with no wording the cum-dividend close (last close before the ex-date)
source: CRSP Data Descriptions Guide (cumulative factor to adjust price, CFACPR); Yahoo Finance adjusted-close methodology; Hull, Options, Futures and Other Derivatives (dividend drops the price by D on the ex-date)

decision: which rows a split / dividend factor multiplies in a backward-adjusted series

options.value: rows dated strictly before the action date (the action date itself is already post-event)
rows up to and including the action date

default: strictly before the action date; the most recent rows stay unadjusted
source: CRSP Data Descriptions Guide (factors apply to prices before the ex-distribution date)

decision: how a backtest's annualized_return is annualised from its daily (periodic) returns

options.value: arithmetic: mean(r) x periods per year (the numerator of the sqrt(periods) Sharpe ratio)
geometric / CAGR: (1 + total_return)^(periods / n) - 1
log: exp(mean(log(1 + r)) x periods) - 1 (or the annual sum of log returns)

default: the task's formula; with none, the arithmetic mean x periods per year (the same mean the sqrt(periods) Sharpe uses; how every silent-worded backtest of this task family was graded correct)
source: Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments ch.5 (arithmetic vs geometric average returns; APR-style annualisation x periods); Sharpe (1994) J. Portfolio Management (annualised mean / annualised std); Bacon, Practical Portfolio Performance Measurement and Attribution ch.2 (annualised return: arithmetic vs compound)

decision: Poisson rate of the weights in the Merton (1976) jump-diffusion series price

options.value: lambda' = lambda (1 + k): w_n = e^{-lambda' T} (lambda' T)^n / n! with r_n = r - lambda k + n ln(1 + k)/T
lambda: w_n = e^{-lambda T} (lambda T)^n / n! (as the task's own formula writes it)

default: the weights the task's formula writes; with no formula lambda' = lambda (1 + k) (Merton 1976)
source: Merton (1976) J. Financial Economics 3, eq. (16); Haug, The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas (2007) s.6.10
